title: Fifth Word Anxiety Over Sustenance And Choosing This World Or The Hereafter

questions.question: Who gives life and keeps it going by giving food?
questions.answer: Allah does.

questions.question: Can life be cared for by someone other than the One who made it?
questions.answer: No. The same One who made life also keeps it going.

questions.question: Which animals are named as weak or not smart but still well fed?
questions.answer: Fish and worms in fruit.

questions.question: Which creatures are named as very weak but given the nicest food?
questions.answer: Babies and young animals.

questions.question: What does this teach about how lawful food comes?
questions.answer: It comes from Allah, not just from strength.

questions.question: What is a person like if he leaves prayer because he is busy getting money or food?
questions.answer: He is like a soldier who leaves his job and goes begging.

questions.question: What is the better way to look for your food after prayer?
questions.answer: Ask Allah for provision and work without depending on people.

questions.question: Why is working for your food in that way called a kind of worship?
questions.answer: Because it is done in a good way, after prayer, and without being a burden to others.

questions.question: What does human nature show people were made for?
questions.answer: Worship.

questions.question: In worldly strength, what small bird are people said to be weaker than?
questions.answer: A sparrow.

questions.question: In knowledge, needs, prayer, and asking Allah, what are people compared to among animals?
questions.answer: Kings and commanders.

questions.question: What happens if a person makes this world the main goal of life?
questions.answer: He becomes low like the smallest bird.

questions.question: What happens if a person makes the Hereafter the main goal and uses this life to prepare for it?
questions.answer: He becomes noble and honored by Allah.

questions.question: At the end, what are the two choices set before the reader?
questions.answer: To live for this world or to live for the Hereafter.

questions.question: From whom should a person ask help to choose the right way?
questions.answer: From Allah, the Most Merciful.

questions.question: What big idea is taught at the start of the passage about life and food?
questions.answer: The One who gives life is also the One who provides food.

questions.question: Why are fish and fruit worms mentioned?
questions.answer: To show that even weak creatures are fed well.

questions.question: Why are infants and baby animals mentioned?
questions.answer: To show that very helpless creatures receive special food.

questions.question: When we compare weak creatures with stronger ones, what lesson do we learn?
questions.answer: Food is not gained only by power or clever plans.

questions.question: If someone skips prayer because of work for money, what mistake is he making?
questions.answer: He is putting earning before obeying Allah.

questions.question: What picture is used to show that mistake?
questions.answer: A soldier leaving his post and begging in the market.

questions.question: What two good things are joined together in the better path?
questions.answer: Praying first and then seeking food in a respectful way.

questions.question: Why is not being a burden on others praised?
questions.answer: Because it is honorable and responsible.

questions.question: What does the passage say about people compared with a sparrow in things needed for worldly life?
questions.answer: People are not strong or skilled like that small bird.

questions.question: In what ways are people given a higher rank than animals?
questions.answer: In knowing, needing, worshipping, and asking Allah.

questions.question: If someone lives only for dunya, what does he become like?
questions.answer: A very low creature.

questions.question: If someone uses dunya to plant for Akhirah, what does he become like?
questions.answer: A high leader and honored servant.

questions.question: What does it mean to use this life as a field for the Hereafter?
questions.answer: It means doing things here to earn reward for later.

questions.question: Does the passage say a person is forced into one path?
questions.answer: No. A person chooses between the two ways.

questions.question: What should a believer do after hearing about the two ways?
questions.answer: Ask Allah for guidance and success.

questions.question: Who is the only true giver of both life and daily provision?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What kind of proof does the passage give from animals?
questions.answer: Weak animals often get food more easily than strong ones.

questions.question: Name one weak creature from the passage that is well fed.
questions.answer: A fish.

questions.question: Name another weak creature from the passage that is well fed.
questions.answer: A worm in fruit.

questions.question: What human example shows special care in food?
questions.answer: Little babies.

questions.question: What does this say about chasing provision with only your own strength?
questions.answer: Strength alone is not what brings provision.

questions.question: Why is leaving prayer for earning a living compared to a soldier doing the wrong thing?
questions.answer: Because he leaves his real duty for something lower.

questions.question: After doing the prayers, how should a person seek provision?
questions.answer: By trusting Allah and working in a good, decent way.

questions.question: Why is that kind of work still valuable in Islam?
questions.answer: Because it can count like worship.

questions.question: What do human nature and the soul’s abilities point to?
questions.answer: That people were created to worship Allah.

questions.question: In everyday worldly abilities, are humans shown as greater or less than a sparrow?
questions.answer: Less.

questions.question: In matters of worship and calling on Allah, are humans shown as low or high?
questions.answer: High.

questions.question: What is the result of making worldly life your biggest goal?
questions.answer: You become low in rank.

questions.question: What is the result of making the Hereafter your biggest goal?
questions.answer: You become honored and close to Allah.

questions.question: What final advice is given after both paths are explained?
questions.answer: Choose the better path and ask Allah to help you.

questions.question: According to the passage, who both creates life and keeps it alive with provision?
questions.answer: Allah.

questions.question: What simple lesson comes from seeing weak creatures receive food?
questions.answer: Allah sends food even to those with little strength.

questions.question: Which is more important for getting lawful provision in the passage: power or helpless need before Allah?
questions.answer: Helpless need before Allah.

questions.question: What is wrong with giving up prayer because of earning a living?
questions.answer: It means forgetting your main duty to Allah.

questions.question: What story-picture shows this wrong choice?
questions.answer: A soldier leaves his place and goes to ask around in the market.

questions.question: What is the right order for a Muslim in the passage?
questions.answer: Pray first, then seek provision.

questions.question: How does the passage describe earning your food without leaning on people?
questions.answer: It is good and honorable.

questions.question: Besides work, what else can that effort become?
questions.answer: A kind of worship.

questions.question: What do a person’s inner qualities show about why people were created?
questions.answer: They show people were made for worship.

questions.question: Compared with a sparrow, how are humans in getting through worldly life?
questions.answer: They are weaker and less able.

questions.question: Compared with animals in worship and dua, how are humans described?
questions.answer: They are like rulers over them.

questions.question: If a person lives only for dunya, what low comparison is given?
questions.answer: He is like the lowest sparrow.

questions.question: If a person aims for Akhirah and uses dunya to prepare, what high comparison is given?
questions.answer: He is like a noble commander.

questions.question: How many paths are placed before the person in the passage?
questions.answer: Two paths.

questions.question: What should be asked from the Most Merciful at the end?
questions.answer: Guidance and success.

questions.question: What truth does the passage teach about the One who made life?
questions.answer: He is also the One who feeds and sustains life.

questions.question: Why does the passage talk about fish, worms, babies, and young animals?
questions.answer: To help us notice that weak ones are cared for with food.

questions.question: What can we understand when weak creatures are fed better than some strong ones?
questions.answer: Provision is from Allah, not simply from muscle or effort.

questions.question: If someone says, “I am too busy working to pray,” what would the passage say about that?
questions.answer: He is choosing wrongly and leaving an important duty.

questions.question: What person in the example acts like that?
questions.answer: A soldier who leaves his duty and goes begging.

questions.question: What is the healthy and respectful way to get your food?
questions.answer: Do your prayers and then work while trusting Allah.

questions.question: Why is going out to earn in that way better than depending on people?
questions.answer: It keeps a person responsible and not a burden.

questions.question: What extra reward can come from that kind of effort?
questions.answer: It can be counted as worship.

questions.question: What do human nature and spiritual gifts tell us about our purpose?
questions.answer: Our purpose is to worship Allah.

questions.question: In worldly action and strength, what bird is used to show human weakness?
questions.answer: A sparrow.

questions.question: In prayer and turning to Allah, what high picture is used for humans?
questions.answer: Leaders among animals.

questions.question: What does a person become like if this world is all he works for?
questions.answer: He becomes low and base.

questions.question: What does a person become like if the Hereafter is his main goal?
questions.answer: He becomes elevated and honored.

questions.question: How should this world be used if the Hereafter is your goal?
questions.answer: As a tool and field to prepare for it.

questions.question: After learning this, what should a Muslim ask Allah for?
questions.answer: Help to choose the right way and do well in it.

questions.question: Who alone gives life and keeps it going with provision?
questions.answer: Allah alone.

questions.question: What examples show that weak creatures can receive plenty of food?
questions.answer: Fish and worms, and also babies and young animals.

questions.question: What does the passage want us to understand from those examples?
questions.answer: Food comes by Allah’s care, not only by strength or planning.

questions.question: What is a person doing if he drops the prayers because he is chasing provision?
questions.answer: He is leaving his real duty.

questions.question: What is he compared to in the passage?
questions.answer: A soldier who leaves his place and begs in the market.

questions.question: What should come before looking for your daily food?
questions.answer: Performing the prayers.

questions.question: How is working for your needs after prayer described?
questions.answer: It is proper, brave, and a kind of worship.

questions.question: Why is it better to go earn than to sit and make others carry you?
questions.answer: Because a person should not be a burden on others.

questions.question: What do a person’s natural and spiritual sides prove?
questions.answer: That people were created for worship.

questions.question: In worldly life skills, are humans pictured as above or below a sparrow?
questions.answer: Below.

questions.question: In knowledge, need, dua, and worship, are humans pictured as low or noble?
questions.answer: Noble.

questions.question: If dunya becomes the main target, what does the passage warn will happen?
questions.answer: A person becomes low like the least bird.

questions.question: If Akhirah becomes the main target, what does the passage promise in rank?
questions.answer: A person becomes high, honored, and close to Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage leave room for choice between the two ways?
questions.answer: Yes. A person may choose either way.

questions.question: What is the best thing to ask from Allah after making that choice?
questions.answer: Guidance and success.
